literal: In the twenty-third year of Tonghe, Shengzong walled Qijin Mountain and founded Zhongjing at Dading Prefecture.
idiomatic: Shengzong's Tonghe year 23 saw Qijin Mountain fortified and Zhongjing established at Dading Prefecture.

literal: It governed nine counties and twenty-three armies, prefectures, and cities.
idiomatic: Zhongjing governed nine counties and twenty-three military prefectures and posts.

literal: Still in early founding and not yet fixed; ding rolls were unverified—only one county is visible: Gaozhou Sanhan County, ten thousand ding.
idiomatic: Because the seat was newly founded, levies were not fully tallied; only Gaozhou's Sanhan County is recorded at 10,000 ding.

literal: Roughly, visible militia ding of the Five Capitals totaled one million one hundred seven thousand three hundred.
idiomatic: In all, the Five Capitals' visible militia rolls came to about 1,107,300 levies.

literal: Liao subject states that can be recorded number fifty-nine; tribute audiences were irregular.
idiomatic: Fifty-nine subject states appear in the records, though tribute missions had no fixed schedule.

literal: When affairs arose the court sent envoys to levy troops, or issued edicts for dedicated campaigns;
idiomatic: In emergencies the court dispatched envoys to raise troops or issued edicts ordering separate expeditions;

literal: Those who did not comply were attacked.
idiomatic: States that refused were punished by force.

literal: Auxiliary forces varied in size at each state's convenience; there was no fixed quota.
idiomatic: Contributed forces followed each realm's means, with no standing quota.

literal: There was also the Iron-Forbidden State: in Shengzong's Chongxi year 17 it begged troops to assist the attack on Western Xia; the edict refused.
idiomatic: The Iron-Forbidden State once asked in Chongxi year 17 to join an attack on Western Xia; the court denied the request.
